title: Distribute and conquer
hints: A conditional type on a naked type parameter runs once *per union member* and unions the results. And `never` vanishes from a union: `"a" | never` is just `"a"`.

MyExclude: for each member of T, keep it if it's *not* assignable to U, otherwise produce `never`. IsNever: `T extends never` on a naked `T` distributes over the empty union and gives `never` — stop the distribution by wrapping both sides in a one-element tuple.
type MyExclude<T, U> = T extends U ? never : T;  type IsNever<T> = [T] extends [never] ? true : false;
